trial_court: Court of Sh. Ankit Mittal, Civil Judge-01 (South) Saket Court, New Delhi
case_name: Dr. Radhey Shyam vs Radhey Shyam
facts_of_case: The respondent had taken a friendly loan of Rs. 1,50,000/- from the petitioner for personal use. The respondent defaulted in paying the interest and issued three cheques which were dishonoured. A legal notice was issued but the respondent did not reply or pay the loan amount.

legal_principles.principle: Where a defendant fails to enter an appearance within the stipulated time, the allegations in the plaint shall be deemed to be admitted and the plaintiff shall be entitled to a decree for any sum not exceeding the amount mentioned in the summons together with interest at the rate specified up to the date of decree and costs.
legal_principles.held: On default of entering the appearance by the defendant, the allegations in the plaint shall be deemed to be admitted and the plaintiff shall be entitled to a decree for any sum, not exceeded the sum mentioned in the summons together with the interest at the rate specified upto the date of decree and costs.
cited_cases: Comba Telecom Ltd. Vs. S. Tel Pvt. Ltd., (2016) 228 DLT 713

legal_principles.principle: A plaintiff is entitled to a decree forthwith under the Scheme of Order 37 CPC where more than 10 days have elapsed after service of summons and none appeared on behalf of the defendant.
legal_principles.held: The present suit has been proceeded u/O XXXVII Rule 2(3) CPC. Since more than 10 days had elapsed after service of summons and none appeared on behalf of the defendant, the plaintiff is entitled to decree forthwith under the Scheme of Order 37 CPC.

outcome.final_order: The court ordered the recovery of Rs. 1,50,000/- along with pendente lite and future interest @ 18% p.a. from the date of disbursement of the loan amount.

use_for_drafting: drafting a summary suit for cheque bounce
advising on recovery of debt from a friend or acquaintance
assisting in drafting a plaint for a friendly loan dispute
